Subject: Re: Discovery — model selection for clinical note extraction

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and a couple asks so we can move to a pilot decision.

Summary of our needs (as discussed):
- High precision extraction of clinical entities and negation detection from clinical notes (many short notes, average 220 tokens).
- PHI-sensitive data; we need private deployment or strong SOC2 + KMS options.
- Target production: ~30 sustained RPS for inference peak windows, bursts to 100 RPS.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you share Redwood-verified perf profiles (TPS, p50/p95 latency with the 220-token distribution) for recommended models?
2) A sample prompt set we can run against our golden questions to sanity-check quality regressions.
3) Any notes on quantization tradeoffs you think are relevant for extraction tasks (quality vs cost).

If you can send the perf sheet and a prompt pack we’ll run a quick internal QC and propose a pilot scope later this week. Also cc'ing our procurement alias for any paperwork.

Thanks,
Mike

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Discovery — inference perf + next steps

Thanks Mike — great to connect. Below is a concise delivery to unblock your QC run plus next steps for a pilot. I attached the Redwood-verified performance profiles and a starter prompt pack tailored to clinical extraction.

1) Quick model recommendations (fit for entity extraction, ordered by quality → cost):
- redwood-7b-structured-q4 (best price/precision for short-context extraction)
- llama-3-13b-instruct (balanced quality, higher latency)
- redwood-70b-qa-q8 (highest recall for edge cases; higher cost)

2) Perf highlights (from our verified bench with your token distribution — avg. 220 tokens per request, batch size=auto):
- redwood-7b-structured-q4:  TPS 120, p50 = 35 ms, p95 = 120 ms
- llama-3-13b-instruct: TPS 55, p50 = 70 ms, p95 = 260 ms
- redwood-70b-qa-q8: TPS 18, p50 = 180 ms, p95 = 430 ms

Notes: TPS here is tokens per second for the runtime configuration we validated (continuous batching, KV cache disabled for cold-start sim). p95 includes model + network tail. We include a performance profile PDF with full percentile breakdown and the test harness settings.

3) Prompt pack & quality regression checks
- Attached: prompt_pack_clinical_v1.jsonl — includes 120 annotated prompts covering entities, negation, and formatting edge cases. Use this to sanity-check any quantized model.
- Recommendation: run the pack against at least two model variants (redwood-7b-structured-q4 and llama-3-13b-instruct) and compute strict F1 on entity spans plus a separate check on negation flips.

4) Quantization notes
- Q4 quantization on structured models has minimal impact on span extraction recall for our tests (<2% F1 delta) but helps TPS substantially.
- Aggressive quantization for 70b reduces cost but increases hallucination risk — we only recommend for batched, non-PHI workloads.

5) Compliance & deployment options
- We can run this as Redwood Private (VPC) with customer KMS and SOC2 evidence. I attached the perf profiles and we can route your security team to laura for docs.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_verified_profiles_20261119.pdf (pdf, 1.2 MB)], [Attachment: prompt_pack_clinical_v1.jsonl (jsonl, 340 KB)]

Next steps:
- Mike: run the prompt pack + share initial QC metrics by EOD Friday (Nov 20).
- Dev: I’ll follow up with a short config note for the pilot infra (target RPS and estimated GPU footprint).
- Laura: can you queue SOC2 + procurement touchpoint after Mike confirms QC?

Thanks — sending links below to the benchmark folder and a short checklist so your team can run the pack.

—
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com

Looping in a couple technical clarifications to make the pilot config concrete.

Mike — quick questions to size the infra:
- Are most requests single-turn extraction (200–250 tokens) or do you expect multi-step prompts with >1k tokens occasionally?
- Do you have a target P99 latency SL A we should optimize for during pilot?

Pilot sizing note (proposal):
- For steady 30 RPS with avg 220 tokens and redwood-7b-structured-q4, estimated requirement: 2x A100-80GB equivalents (with autoscale to 4x for bursts to 100 RPS). That projection assumes our continuous batching and prefix caching are enabled.

If you prefer, we can provide a short test harness (container + runner) that runs the prompt pack and emits F1, latency percentiles, and token cost estimates — this is what we used to generate the attached perf PDF.
